sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`stats` gives a flat count per bucket — `by_status`, `by_size`, `by_tree`, `by_pass` —
where `by_tree` counts all items in a tree regardless of status. There is no percent-
complete and no per-tree open-vs-done split, so "how far along am I, and which tree is
lagging" cannot be answered without exporting `list --json` and pivoting it by hand. For
a tool whose stated purpose is roadmap management, that is the first question a user asks.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` — `cmd_stats`
- `src/slicer/model.py` — a cross-tabulation helper if one is cleaner than inline

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `stats --json` includes a done/total and a percent-complete.
2. It includes a per-tree done-vs-open breakdown.
3. The existing flat counts are unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add a completion summary (done, total, percent) and a status-by-tree cross-tabulation to
the `stats` payload and text. Keep the existing buckets so nothing breaks.

**Not in this slice:** burndown over time or diff-since-a-git-ref — that wants history
this tool does not keep yet (see S20).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `stats` answers per-tree progress and overall completion at a glance.
